newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam plans to rein in population growth by 2005.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam plans to rein in population growth by 2005.

text.p: Vietnam said on Friday the government aimed to stabilise the country's population at just over 88 million by 2005 after several years of rapid growth.

The official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said the latest estimate of the nation's population was 77 million, a rise of about 14 percent from 1991, and two million higher than the previous official figure.
"The population growth rate is now...2.3 percent per year, with every couple urged not to have more than two children," the agency said.

Under Vietnamese law, local authorities may impose a fine on families which have more than two children in what is one of the most densely populated and poorest countries in the world. The average income per head in Vietnam is around $275 a year.
VNA said the average number of children per woman in the fertile age group had dropped to 3.1 in 1994 from six just over 30 years ago.
